card.band: 4 h. Several levers: algorithmic, memory layout, parallelism across 8 cores. A frontier agent usually finds the incremental evaluation but not the layout work. A weaker model breaks equivalence. The licence must be confirmed before bundling, though the generated instances avoid shipping the data.
card.cheat: Returning cached optima for published instances. The instances are generated from hidden seeds, and the equivalence gate checks full solutions.
card.grading: A hard gate: results must equal the reference on generated instances (exact objective for the deterministic solver, an identical seeded trajectory for the search). Score is the wall-clock median speedup against our reference, 2^u-1. Hidden instances are drawn from unseen seeds and sizes.
card.reference: We write an optimised implementation (bitset DP, incremental delta evaluation). The measured speedup S is set at calibration. No upstream reference was found.
card.source: https://people.brunel.ac.uk/~mastjjb/jeb/info.html (OR-Library, cutting and BQP formats), licence unverified (not found)
card.task: /app ships a correct but slow C++ or Python baseline of a two-dimensional guillotine cutting solver and a binary quadratic programming local search. Instances use the OR-Library file formats but are generated by a seeded generator, not the published files. The agent makes both faster without changing results.

source_notes: Old and widely mirrored, so instance data is memorable and the optimum tables may be recallable. Better as a multi-problem research suite than a single-problem task. Not on already_known. CPU-only and small instances, which fits the sandbox.

facts.claim: OR-Library (J.E. Beasley, Brunel) hosts two-dimensional cutting data (unconstrained guillotine gcut, constrained guillotine cgcut, non-guillotine) and unconstrained binary quadratic programming (BQP) data sets

Licence: OR-Library states the MIT licence applies to all its material, with copyright (c) 2010 J E Beasley, and no per-dataset exceptions are stated on the page (the seed's 'licence unverified' is resolved)

Unconstrained guillotine cutting: 13 data files gcut1 to gcut13 (12 from Beasley 1985 Table 1, plus one from Table 2); file format is number of pieces, stock length and width, then length, width, value per piece
Optimal values for gcut1 to gcut12 are published in the 1985 JORS paper; no optimal value is given for gcut13 on the OR-Library page

BQP: 7 data files (bqpgka, bqp50, bqp100, bqp250, bqp500, bqp1000, bqp2500); objective is maximisation of sum q(i,j)x(i)x(j) over binary x; sparse text format with n and non-zero count per problem; no best-known or optimal values published on the page
The seed's claim that no upstream reference implementation exists was not checked against GitHub or package registries; only the OR-Library pages were verified

full_card.band: Tier 4 h. Levers: incremental evaluation (frontier usually finds), memory layout and parallelism (usually missed), equivalence (weaker models break it). Partial credit from the speedup curve. No dated public evidence of agent performance on this kind of work.
full_card.build_cost: About 3-5 days: write both baselines, reference solvers, generator, equivalence harness, and calibrate speedup. No smoke build exists because there is no git source.
full_card.deliverable: Faster solver code for both problems with identical results: exact objective for the cutting DP, identical seeded trajectory for the BQP search.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Cached optima useless: instances are generated from hidden seeds and the gate compares full solutions. Must pin RNG and move-selection rules in the spec so a different valid implementation can match the trajectory; otherwise the gate encodes the reference's structure. Block editing tests or build config, and reject vendored binaries.
full_card.grading_surface: Generated instances from hidden seeds and sizes; exact-equality gate on objective (DP) and on the full search trajectory (BQP); score is median wall-clock speedup vs reference, 2^u-1.
full_card.local_fit: CPU-only, small instances, 8 cores, 16 GB: fits the sandbox. No network needed at run time.
full_card.lookup: partial: Beasley 1985 unconstrained guillotine DP and Glover-Kochenberger-Alidaee BQP tabu search are published and recallable in outline; no complete public port of the same generator or reference was found in searches, and GitHub was not searched.
full_card.provenance: OR-Library (J.E. Beasley), MIT licence, copyright 2010; instance formats from gcut (1985 JORS) and bqp (gka/Beasley) sets. Data files not shipped; generator is ours.
full_card.reference: Not found upstream. We write it: bitset DP for cutting plus incremental delta evaluation for BQP; layout and 8-core parallelism as further levers. S set at calibration.
full_card.ships: Our slow C++ or Python baseline for a guillotine cutting solver and a BQP local search, a seeded generator in OR-Library formats, an equivalence harness. No OR-Library data files.
full_card.similarity: Max l0 neighbour cosine 0.13 (S-im-062); no crowded-list overlap; not a speedup of an existing public task.

Band.why: Several levers and a weaker-model separation are plausible, but there is no dated public evidence and the scope may be small for 4 h.

Build.why: Roughly 3-5 days to write both baselines, reference, generator and harness.

Fit.why: CPU-only, small instances, fits 8 cores and 16 GB.

Hor.why: Two modest algorithms fit a 4 h tier; a larger tier or more problems would be needed for sustained work.

Lic.why: OR-Library MIT licence confirmed; data files are not shipped.

Multi.why: Two problems, multiple sizes, and a speedup curve give steady partial credit.

Nov.why: Max neighbour cosine 0.13 and no crowded-list overlap.

Real.why: OR-Library formats and published algorithms are real and MIT-licensed, but the baseline and reference are written by us, not a real codebase.

Ref.why: We write the reference; no upstream exists, so S is only a calibration measurement.

Seal.why: Hidden seeds and our own reference keep the oracle and reference out of reach; the algorithms are recallable, which is scored under Band.

Surf.why: Unlimited seeded generator with an executable equivalence oracle over full solutions and trajectories.

spike_plan.kill_if: Speedup over naive is under 2x on either problem, trajectories cannot be matched deterministically across implementations, or the BQP search cannot be pinned to a spec-level RNG and move rule.
spike_plan.pass_if: Fast versions are at least 3x faster than naive on both problems, outputs match on all sampled seeds, and timings vary by under 10% across runs.
steps: Write a seeded generator for gcut-format (pieces, stock, value) and bqp-format (n, sparse q entries) instances at two sizes each.
Write a naive guillotine DP and a naive BQP local search with a fixed RNG and move order in C++, and time them.
Write the reference-style versions: bitset DP and incremental delta evaluation; time them against the naive versions.
Check that naive and fast versions produce identical objectives (DP) and identical trajectories (BQP) over 50 seeds.
Run each binary 5 times to check wall-clock median stability and determinism.
Test whether 8-thread parallelism gives a measurable gain on the BQP search without breaking the trajectory.

v1.summary: The OR-Library cutting and BQP data sets are real and their licence is now confirmed as MIT (copyright J E Beasley, 2010), so the bundling gate passes once data files are not shipped. The task is viable as a two-problem optimization suite, but it depends on pinning the BQP RNG and move rule in the spec, and the reference is ours, so Band and Ref are only moderate.

v2.note: OR-Library formats and the MIT licence are confirmed, but the system being optimised is two small solvers we would write and make slow on purpose. That is a puzzle rather than a real codebase, and it fails the Real bar. Each problem has one textbook lever: the Beasley DP bitset or memo, and incremental delta evaluation for the BQP. Requiring an identical seeded BQP trajectory also rules out most algorithmic levers, so the gate largely encodes our reference's structure. A weaker model would likely find delta evaluation, so the frontier lead of 0.20 is doubtful. Not long-horizon at 4 h.
